root_idea.summary: The root centers on reaching an extreme or becoming fully immersed in something, concretely sinking into water.
root_idea.development: From sinking or drowning, the lexical field extends to complete inclusion, being overwhelmed, vehement exertion, overflowing or filling, and figurative immersion in burdens or favors.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Presented under the singular passive-participle citation form.

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to sink in water; to drown.
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively, with active, passive, and imperfect forms in the Quran; the result is submersion or drowning in water.
In the Quranic construction in which drowning overtakes a person, referring to the state or event of submersion.
In 79:1, it describes the vehement pulling out of souls, with غَرْقًا functioning in place of the verbal noun of أَغْرَقَ.

senses.definition: Drowned; caused to sink in water.
senses.usage_conditions: A passive participle used substantivally for those who have been or are to be drowned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sink in water; to drown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The primary Form I use is described as sinking under water, with death occurring in the fullest description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go down and disappear in lands or tracts of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with فِي البِلَادِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take a draught of milk or another drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used with the noun غُرْقَةٌ for the draught taken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become free from want or need.
Figurative immersion or being overwhelmed in affliction or in another's favor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a metaphorical extension of sinking in water, as in being immersed in hardship or in someone's beneficence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kill by drowning; by extension, to kill.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The specialized account concerns a newborn drowned in birth fluid or killed when fluid or mucus enters the air passages.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ornament with silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a bridle or the scabbard of a sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove the غِرْقِئ, the inner covering of an egg.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with the egg as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near or approach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in constructions such as غَارَقَنِي كَذَا, and figuratively of death becoming near.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become obligatory or inevitable, said of an onslaught or event.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative use applied to an impending occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To annul or destroy one's good works through acts of disobedience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of causing something to sink or be lost.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be overrun and overcome by people or beasts multiplying against one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction is used with people or beasts as the force overcoming someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To outstrip another in sprightliness or speed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the description of a horse outstripping a fox.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive a spear so deeply that the part entering its iron head disappears into the person pierced.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension describing extreme penetration caused by force and speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a cup.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a cup or drinking vessel as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw a bow or arrow to the utmost extent; hence to exceed the usual bounds or act immoderately.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bow construction refers to an exceptionally forceful draw; the extended use applies to speech, conduct, or another matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mix among competitors and then outstrip them; figuratively, to overcome an opponent in dispute.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a horse among other horses and of prevailing in an altercation or litigation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take up the whole of a breast-girth or belly-girth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a large-bellied camel whose body makes the girth too narrow.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take in the whole breath with a vehement inhalation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with النَّفَسَ as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To engross or occupy the gaze completely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression describes beauty that diverts observers from looking at anything else.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take in, comprise, include, or occupy altogether and wholly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the grammatical use of universal inclusion of a genus.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exceed the usual degree in laughing; to laugh immoderately.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with laughter or another activity in which a person goes beyond the normal measure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the eyes to fill with tears or shed tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One reported nuance is that the eyes fill with tears without overflowing; the lexical image is of eyes as though drowned in tears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Submerged in water or overcome by water without having died.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Some authorities distinguish this state from غَرِيقٌ, which denotes death by drowning; other reports distinguish being overcome before sinking from having sunk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dead by sinking in water; drowned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A participial designation for one who has died through submersion; authorities also report variation in the distribution of غَرِقٌ and غَرِيقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The desperate, sincere prayer of one on the brink of destruction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression likening urgency and sincerity in prayer to that of a drowning person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go to the utmost degree in drinking wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use describing extreme immersion in wine-drinking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Land in the utmost state of irrigation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective for land saturated or exceptionally well supplied with water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deeply in debt or overwhelmed by trials.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of a person submerged under financial or other burdens.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Frightened so that one's voice is stopped short.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression إِنَّهُ لَغَرِقُ الصَّوْتِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single draught or a small quantity of milk or another beverage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is غُرَقٌ; the sources especially associate the term with milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overwhelmed by another's favors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression أَنَا غَرِيقُ أَيَادِيكَ, literally likening favors to a flood in which one is drowned.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A reported name for a certain bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attestation is explicitly described as not established.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A medicinal substance, also called أَغَارِيقُونٌ, identified with an ancient Greek drug or the root of a plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as an antidote and medicinal attenuant; the term is a borrowed technical name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that casts her young and does not incline toward or care for it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a she-camel after casting her young, with associated refusal of milking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ornamented with silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a bridle or the scabbard of a sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Obligatory, in the expression رمضانُ مُغَارِقٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional lexical expression concerning observance of Ramadan.

cautions: Authorities differ in how غَرِقٌ and غَرِيقٌ distribute the meanings 'submerged' and 'dead by drowning'; both reported distinctions are preserved.
The reported bird-name غِرْيَاقٌ is explicitly of uncertain attestation.
The figurative meanings involving affliction and favors are broader Classical Arabic extensions and are not assigned to the Quranic occurrence of غَرَقٌ itself.
